# Informed functional-boundary source study

This is bounded public-source evidence for the ordinary
[#80 decision](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/80#issuecomment-6009479668).
[Initial context](context.md), [independent predictions](predictions-before.json)
and [first source inventory](first-files.json) precede every study CLI command.
The author had repository, Issue, code and design-document context, including the
concurrently authored functional Reference. This is not a blind model benchmark.

[Registration](session.json) retains ten complete first projects and two complete
source repairs, with **44 actual CLI observations** and untouched raw streams.
Every project explicitly selects constitutional edition 2026. No source uses
more than two quantum bits. The fixed existing CLI/native bytes were checked
before and after each invocation. No compiler/Lean build, corpus, library,
example, maximum-size case or generic QFT source was changed.

The first command driver incorrectly used `check --sized <project>`. Ten JSON
and two text commands returned real usage failures before any source judgment;
they remain in the [first capture](observations-first/capture.json). Those are
observer command-authoring errors. The [explicit follow-up](followup-before.json)
records the correction to `sized check --entry=main::main --module=main=PATH`
before the [appended observations](observations-followup/capture.json).
This adapter shares selected-source preparation; agreement is not evidence of
independently implemented checking rules.

| Project | First finite observation | Correct sized adapter observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complete first-order call | Accept; run returns `1` | Accept |
| Missing Unit argument, then attempted call | Arity rejection | Same arity rejection |
| Ordinary local shadows global callable | Local-value category rejection | Same category rejection |
| Tuple carrying Q<Unit> used as callee | Local-value category rejection | Same category rejection |
| Tuple carrying Q<Unit> used as provider | Runtime-provider category rejection | Same category rejection |
| Static XX description used on two owners | Primitive-provider refusal before intended control | Same earlier refusal |
| Original owner used twice | Primitive-provider refusal before ownership control | Same earlier refusal |
| Ordinary Bit condition | Accept; run returns `1` | Unsupported runtime expression |
| Unmeasured quantum condition | Expected Bit, found Q<Bit> | Same type rejection |
| Explicit observation, then ordinary condition | Accept; run returns `0` | Unsupported runtime expression |

Two first sources attempted `then_op(x,x)`, but the existing provider boundary
requires an ordinary source function. Their actual diagnostic and first sources
remain untouched. The [next context](context-after-first.md) explains the two
complete `attempt-02` projects: `wrapped_x` supplies that function and only the
provider names change. Reuse then checks and runs as `00` through the finite
route. Owner duplication reaches the intended ownership rejection on both
routes: `quantum ownership q has already been consumed`. The sized adapter
still rejects concrete `then_op` construction as unsupported; no weaker route
or successful generic provider theorem is inferred.

[Assessment](assessment.json) separates matched predictions, earlier refusals,
command-authoring errors and current concrete emitter limits. The four tiny
execution distributions equal the prior mathematical expectations from X,
X squared and destructive Z observation. This does not establish arbitrary
reference behavior, scalar phase, axis order, source preservation or native
compilation/runtime correctness. Empty main in the open Q<Unit> counterexamples
does not execute those open bodies. Actual resolved category checks, rather
than syntax-only closure rejection, are the recorded controls. No universal
closure-capture proof or new production defect is claimed.

The [metadata check](metadata-check-first.json) passed on its first run:
40 sessions, 55 snapshots and 911 observations, with no recorded command executed.
Source/manifest and raw-stream hashes were also verified while registering this
session. The initial current-baseline constitutional comparison and separate
[trusted continuity follow-up](trusted-continuity-followup.json) are preserved.
The supplied source baseline `5bcc36f8` is distinct from trusted constitutional
base `faa5cfb5`. QS, PR, quantitative RS and EXACT broader obligations remain pending;
the two protected scoped QLV1 guarantees are unchanged. This ordinary study
provides no Guardian judgment, guarantee admission, Issue closure or release gate.
